title: Query Rewriting, Multi-Hop and Graph RAG
summary: Basic RAG embeds the user's words and fetches the nearest chunks. That fails for follow-up questions, vague phrasing, questions needing several facts, and questions about a whole corpus. This lesson covers the main extensions, their maths and their costs.
objectives: Rewrite conversational and ambiguous queries, and fuse results from multiple rewrites
Explain HyDE and show with cosine similarity why a hypothetical answer can retrieve better than the question
Compute how per-hop failure compounds in multi-hop questions and decompose a question into sub-queries
Describe graph RAG, estimate its indexing cost and say when it beats vector search
Choose a technique from the observed failure, and count the latency and cost it adds
prerequisites: You should know the basic RAG pipeline ([How RAG Works](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/rag-architecture)), hybrid search and RRF ([Hybrid Search and Reranking](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/hybrid-and-reranking)) and the cost of chunk-based prompts. Basic probability (independent events multiply) is used.
